recommendation_summary: Right now: schedule the existing command with cron on the always-on Linux machine to run once a night, early enough to finish before 08:00, and append stdout/stderr to a log. If a morning report is missing, rerun the same command by hand. Nothing extra is offered alongside it. Two things are still open: nobody has checked the interpreter or paths on that machine, and nothing alerts anyone when a run fails.

labels.Requirements and who asked: A report ready by 08:00 from the existing three-minute Python command; you asked. An Airflow-on-Kubernetes worker, scheduler, and deployment split, plus future-proofing, came from peer practice and available budget.
labels.Deleted: Airflow, Kubernetes, separate workers, a scheduler service, and a deployment platform for this export.
labels.Bottleneck: The laptop is asleep overnight, so the command never starts. Successful runs are already correct, and running the command again safely replaces that night's output.
labels.Checked myself: Only your description: a three-minute command, no downstream jobs, safe rerun, missing runs when the laptop sleeps, an always-on Linux machine you already administer, a deadline of 08:00, and a flexible start time. I did not inspect that machine.

note: The reply fills in all four record lines before recommending, and its recommendation is a bounded cron job on the existing server with no orchestration stack.
